Even weeds have issues growing in my yard!  So, when it rained, the yard would turn into a really gross and sticky red mud mess. My first attempt for me to walk as well as keeping my dog's paws cleaner (and not tracking mud in the house after it rained) was the RV plastic rugs and that works, but because of the change in height from the clay/soil to the concrete pad, I had tripped a few times when moving things around in the yard. These are also cushy, so when I step off the concrete pad, it's like being on plush carpet in a way.  I have picked them up, hosed them off and they are very sturdy and durable for my outdoor use.

With only one coffee drinker in the family we didn't need a 3 quart coffee boiler for camp coffee. What we needed was an inexpensive, well built, 3-4 quart container for boiling water for cocoa, making coffee with a a one-cup Melita drip coffee cone, reconstituting instant oatmeal, and for easily adding hot water to our camp showers. The Graniteware coffee boiler was exactly what we needed. We fill it, use what we need for breakfast, then turn it off and set it aside. Later, especially if the day is cloudy or the solar shower water has cooled later in the evening, we'll add some more water, reheat, then add the hot water to our solar showers. We split it between two 2.5 gallon solar showers. The Graniteware Coffee Boiler was exactly what we needed and we've had absolutely no problems. Be sure to use a hot glove or pad when pouring if you just took it off the fire or the stove.

I also use it in my backyard for replenishing water in my smoker. I've learned the temperature of the smoker remains more constant when I add boiling water to the water reservoir. My gas grill has a separate pot burner and it is right next to my smoker. I just fill the coffee boiler with water, place it on the burner, and have hot water at the ready when I need to replenish the smoker.

StoreYourBoard Replacement 12 Inch Balloon Wheels Kayak Dolly and Sand Carts, Big Beach Buggy Inflatable Tires We loved the Rio Wonder Wheeler concept, but it didn't work so great in practice. When loaded, it was very difficult to pull over the sand. We then looked at higher-priced ones with balloon wheels, knowing that those would work better on soft sand. I convinced my husband to try these wheels on the Wonder Wheeler first. We followed the advice of other reviewers and bought a 36" length - 3/8" diameter steel rod from ACE (couldn't find one at Home Depot) and 4 metal flat washers to fit the rod (which would be used as new axle). We drilled a hole 1/2 inch from both ends using a titanium drill bit (the carbide one we bought was useless). We used 1/2" pvc pipe cut to the width of the new wheels. We inflated the tires to 4 lbs. with an electric pump; removed linch pins from original axle (don't lose these or plastic bushings), removed original big plastic wheels, bushings, and axle.
To assemble with new tires: 1) We inserted new axle; 2) then the original bushings (with end protrusion cut off); 3) then a metal washer; 4) new tire with pvc inserted through center; 5) another washer; and 6) inserted original linch pins through drilled holes (repeat steps 2-6 on other side). It now works like a dream and saved us several hundred dollars since we didn't have to buy a new cart.
text_fidelity_b: StoreYourBoard Replacement 12 Inch Balloon Wheels Kayak Dolly and Sand Carts, Big Beach Buggy Inflatable Tires

Seemed like an easy, lighter way of having a nice lounge chair for the beach or picnic. Didn’t turn out that way.

MAYBE it was the lack of a breeze the day we tried it, but in reality, you’re doing all the work. My wife (who is in great shape, can run easily, and fit) ran to try to get enough air inside. It didn’t really work. It actually looks fuller than it feels or is (in the pictures). She tried 3 different times to run and get enough air inside.

But each time it came away not full enough. She’d sit on it (I’m heavier so didn’t even try) and her backside is ON the ground. Yes, her weight pushes the air and makes it look fuller, but she is literally sitting ON the ground - it’s hard and not comfortable. I’m not including the picture of her looking at me and pouting.

In the end we were really disappointed. We are going to try it again - we are looking for a windy day - maybe that’ll do it. But when you’re already running to get it filled, we’re thinking wind will make it harder and you’ll be fighting wind with this giant sail. Anyways, we are disappointed. Can’t recommend.

text_fidelity_a:
Currie Technologies Power Kit I was gifted this from a good friend of mine. Wow! It took 4 hours to install it on my Cannondale Mt Bike. I have tested it on very steep paved roads around my house and it works very well. The battery is very strong for about the 1st 2-3 miles on the hilly area. After that it will start to get a little weaker but still last me about 8 miles with hills. I weigh 216 pounds and I was running it on 2.1 knobby tires on a bike specifically designed for mountain biking - i.e. not road riding. I took it on single track to see how well it would do with some hills, does great! After having it for a couple of months, I got a flat - slow leak. I purchased a thorn resistant tire, Slime tube and Mr Tuffy liners. As other people have said, you do not want to get a flat. But I also carry all of the tools necessary to fix it out on the road just in case. I am no dummy, I have ridden thousands of road and single track miles through the years and flats are a way of life.

I can not over emphasize the ABSOLUTE JOY in riding this thing!! I had lost interest in biking because you always had to get all dolled up just to go for a ride. Not anymore. I wear jeans, Carhartt jacket if its cold and tennis shoes. Ha! I love it. Snap the battery in and I am good to go! What a great way to run to the grocery or hardware store or...

I purchased the second battery. Well worth the $100+. I can now go for a ride and when the first battery dies, click over to the second one and work my way home. I have been riding it on rough ATV trails here in Arizona and beating the heck out of the system. My rim has stayed true and the rack and batteries stay snug.

As a rap up... JOY in riding! Now I am always riding down hill. That use to be one of the things I loved about biking in Colorado where I lived. You ride up so you can ride down. Now the flat stretches are like down hills!! Woohoo! LOVE IT! I feel like a kid again... and it gets me out of the house.

Happy trails...
text_fidelity_b: Currie Technologies Power Kit

text_fidelity_a:
Greallthy Bike Bell Classic Brass Bicycle Bell for Bike Ring Bell with Loud Sound Bells for Road Mountain Bike Handlebars Adults This bell has a nice, piercing, loud, distinctive ring. It is perfect for two lane trails shared by bicyclists, pedestrians, runners, families with strollers, etc. This bell is very effective at warning people ahead that a cyclist is approaching, and they instantly move or stay in their lane so the cyclist can pass unseen on their left.

The clapper is spring loaded requiring the cyclist to allow the lever to snap at the bell. However, under constant ringing, this can potentilly cause irritation to the bellringer's thumb. Thus the reason for only 4 stars instead of 5.
The clapper must "snap" in order for the bell to ring.

I would suggest gloves covering the thumb in winter, and otherwise practicing a technique whereby the thumbnail does most of the interaction with the spring mechanism. One could probably also wear some sort of protective bandaide or other covering on the thumb. The user will have to decide what is best for their circumstances.

There are other bells easier to ring, but this one is very loud and distinctive, and for me, worth the inconvenience of learning the "thumbnail technique."

UPDATE TO MY INITIAL REVIEW
I love this bell, and I would definitely buy it again. PLEASE NOTE: I added a modification that I would like to share.
Using Wedgewood Contact Cement, I attached a strip of tough polyester fabric to the metalic ringer mechanism. This tough but soft fabric protects the thumb from chaffing when ringing the bell (Please see photo). I suggest that a small strip of soft leather would work just as well and perhaps be even more durable. With this easy improvement, I can now raise my rating from 4 to 5 stars.
text_fidelity_b: Greallthy Bike Bell Classic Brass Bicycle Bell for Bike Ring Bell with Loud Sound Bells for Road Mountain Bike Handlebars Adults

had it about 2 weeks, but have already lost several pounds and my jeans
are getting looser, so I know the inches are coming off. The features

want to mention, that this is a huge machine, it is not for a small space,
even though it is possible to fold-up the deck, it is very, very heavy,

as it weighs almost 300 pds. We also have a bowflex weight machine and
now have turned a small spare bedroom into a workout room, next we are
planning to put a flat-screen tv in there, so that will be an incentive
to not be a couch potatoes and to workout and watch our favorite shows and
movies, and get into shape during the long cold winter. If you do choose
to order this product, and choose free shipping, it will take 3 to 4 weeks
to get the machine. But it will save you around $200 for the free shipping
and well worth the wait.

WASING Outdoor Inflatable Lounger Nylon Fabric Beach Lounger Convenient Compression Air Bag Hangout Bean Bag Portable Dream Chair WS-InCOUCH-Blue I originally watched a viral video on facebook and saw that this type of lounger was available. I was curious about it. When this arrived in the mail, my husband immediately set it up and had me sit down in it. Instead of shaking it out (like you do with a garbage bag) he put it in front of a box fan and let it air up very quickly. Then you twist up the end and buckle it. It's extremely easy to use and light weight. It feels like a big balloon, but the material is a lot thicker.

When you sit on it, it feels like laying on a boat. It's soft, the air holds you up so you feel like you are floating. If you lay in the middle, go to reach for something, it will tilt back and fourth and feel like you are swaying on a boat in the water. My kids tried sitting on it and ended up sliding down inside it, so it's not really meant for little guys unless they sit on it like a chair or with someone. The more people on it however means the air escapes faster. If the air starts to escape after a while (an hour with one adult and two kids on it) then it is easy to fix that problem. Simply unbuckle the end, twist it a little tighter and re-buckle it. Then it's back to being nice and tight. When you are done it's easy to fold back down and put away.

This is such a neat idea for taking with you outdoors especially. It's rather long, my husband is around 6 1/2 feet tall and he can stretch out nicely on it. The material will make you feel sweaty after long periods in it, so just be aware when you are choosing how to sit on it or what to wear when you do. It's a nice luxury to take with you anywhere. Plus you don't need a pump to fill up the lounger.

Zippo HeatBank 9s Plus Rechargeable Hand Warmer All of the Zippo hand warmers are offered on this listing. Though some of them look similar, they are not all the same. The one that I have is the 9-Hour Plus model. Make sure you are reading the review for the hand warmer you are interested in.

This device, being produced by Zippo, historically a lighter manufacturer, has the look and feel of a large cigarette lighter. Even the power button is located for thumb operation and is configured much like you’d use a lighter. That’s kind of cool, actually. The feel in the hand is very nice and comfortable. When the power button is depressed for 3+ seconds, the heater comes on at level 1, side one. There are six total heat levels that involve levels one through three, single sided of the unit, and one through three with both sides heating. I can tell you that I was totally amazed at how quickly the unit heated up. Almost instantly you feel significant heat. It cools back down almost as quickly. While the unit does not have a pouch with it, like some similar devices of other brands, I’d consider that it’s not likely to burn you unless you kept it on the high setting right against the skin for a significant amount of time. However, I would not consider this a device for young children. The detachable lanyard, which does not show in the pictures, was a stroke of genius! It measures 18 inches long. You can wear it around your neck at, say, a sporting event that you’d be at for a while in cool temperatures, and be able to detach the device from the lanyard with the latch, turn it on and put in a pocket or pass it to a friend, and then attach it again. Just a great convenience. And, of course, the fact that it has two ports for charging external devices. It only comes with one short charging cord however, the Micro USB that it takes to charge the device itself. Of course you could use it to charge a compatible Micro USB device. IOS users will have to furnish a cord. I just really like this device and find it very useful. Made in China.

text_fidelity_a:
M-Wave Bicycle Cycling Bag Since three vastly different items are in one listing: This is for the individual panniers. They seem solid enough. A bit of a loose seam or thread here or there, seen a lot worse. They have a good bit of space inside, I reckon 3 2-liter soda bottles a side with some stuff along the sides, but it'll be wonky because of the round bottom. The design of the top makes them water resistant, it's not a zipper. The stiffening material is thicker than I expected, will definitely provide protection and support for fairly heavy items. The clips and D-rings don't feel cheap or fragile.

The problems:

I ordered two and got two left-side panniers instead of a matched pair. I didn't even IMAGINE this would be a problem. Title, bullet points and description all need to say "left side only" if that's what it is, AND THE RIGHT SIDE OPTION NEEDS TO BE IN THE SAME LISTING. In any case I don't think heel striking will be a problem, they just look weird.

The top clips are sized for rails no more than 9mm(based on the diameter of the inner clearing, measured by caliper) while the side rails on an Ibera Touring Carrier Plus are 10.5mm. So it only clips on with the first clearing, not very strongly. They also come contracted shut- I had to stretch them out by putting 11.5mm thick pens in each one and leaving them overnight(see attached image.) Now I can at least get the clips on over the rail.

The next problem is that the Ibera rack has no good place to hook the stabilizing bungee. I will need to hook it somewhere weird, which means the panniers can't be taken off with one hand which is a disappointment.

I will try them a couple of times carrying groceries, the purpose I got them for. Their fate is up to how well they do the job.
text_fidelity_b: M-Wave Bicycle Cycling Bag

Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in)) I've been using a Fitbit One for years now. Really love it. But I wanted to get the pulse tracking feature, so purchased the Charge HR recently.

I do love it for the HR monitor, and sleep tracking is a lot easier on the HR (having to put on that wristband to track via the One was an added annoyance). And the caller ID feature is cool.

But there are two things I don't like as well. First, I have a very petite wrist (small bone/frame). The Charge HR looks huge on my wrist, and really doesn't sit well. The inflexible part with the face sticks out beyond my wrist, where on someone with a bigger wrist it would flex where it needs to bend around. Hard to explain!

The other thing, which is probably related, is that when I wear a winter coat, the sleeve pushes the FB down on my wrist where it digs in and hurts.

This isn't significant unless you are competing against others rather than just against yourself like I do, but I think the Charge HR counts more steps than my One does. I haven't changed my routine, but I find I'm hitting my 10,000 much earlier in the day than before.

Oh, and I have to charge the HR more frequently than I did the One.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in))

The Skill Board Mini Beginner to Pro - Wooden Balance Board for Adults Bundle - Incl. Balance Trainer for All Sports, Gym, Standing Desk, or Yard Games, 2x Fitness Balls, Ball Pump and more First, I have to admit, we only used this The Skill Board Mini Beginner to Pro - Wooden Balance Board for Adults Bundle once since arriving. It arrived at the same point my wife and I got sick (we’ve been down for a few weeks), so it’s been in the corner since unpacking and had only one test run. My pics would normally be of the product fully unwrapped and ready for use and/or in use.

But in these pictures you see the size of the bundle included. Pictures of the set show the number of pieces including the two balls, the cushion, and the board (dark brown flat item), and thickness of the board. “Out of the box,” if you will, this The Skill Board Mini Beginner to Pro - Wooden Balance Board for Adults Bundle is a great deal with multiple pieces offering an athlete or anyone working out several options - the cushion is about our speed for beginning, but I know with the balls you can make it harder or easier based on how big the ball is you choose to use, or how much you fill it. The number of items included in the bundle alone makes it a great deal in our book. We have had a previous, similar workout board that only included the board and cushion (to be fair, it was half the price), but while we truly enjoyed that set, we were unable to move up if we wanted without buying more. So that you get as much here as you do is a plus.

We only unwrapped the cushion and platform for our initial test run, and found them both to be excellent for our needs. The thickness of the board made us both comfortable and with a listed weight up to 300 lbs., even with the extra weight I’m working off I am safe and comfortable on the board. We found the cushion to be easy to get inflated and hold the air. Having had one before we knew how to use it and were quickly getting on and off and balancing. We always use ours for both standing on and as a platform for planking and like the challenge. We have not (as of yet) put the non-skid surface on (again, we’ve been down), but have not decided either way if we’ll use it, but we have it for when we are ready.

We are also looking forward to trying the two balls. At this point neither of us is comfortable yet to try, so we’re unable to speak to it, but we love that this is an option to move into once we are ready. In the end we are very pleased with the bundle and feel this The Skill Board Mini Beginner to Pro - Wooden Balance Board will help us get back up and going once we are recovered. Just that test run reminded us how much we love this kind of core workout and how well it worked for us in the past. We’re happy to be able to do this again and believe the The Skill Board Mini Beginner to Pro - Wooden Balance Board for Adults Bundle will be great moving forward.

text_fidelity_a:
Men Waders Waterproof Chest Waders Bootfoot Chest Wader Light Hunting Fly Fishing Waders for Men with Boots Nylon/PVC Wader Camouflage/Brown 8-14 I needed a new pair of waders to replace the ones I ripped to shreds when trimming mangroves in our wetlands. It turns out that the old ones couldn't handle some of the spikes and thorns encountered in our Southwest Florida location. While the leaks did help me cool off when in the water you have to be careful of flesh-eating bacteria down here. If a spike/thorn comes through your pants it will probably lodge in your skin. That is not something that I want to deal with.

For a big guy like me (6'3" and 235 lbs) I was very happy to find that they fit so well. The weak spot tends to be the suspenders which normally don't lock properly or fall apart quickly. The clips on these locked up good and tight so I didn't have to worry about losing my coverage. However whether it's backup for my waders or for the tactical pants I wear with boots tromping around in the wetlands, I have a bright orange pair of Carrhart clip-on suspenders to keep my britches on nice and tight. Some of the surplus military pants that come with suspenders fail immediately.

Two obstacles I always watch out for when chest deep in our brackish water are cottonmouths and alligators. There is a large 12' bull alligator we often see crossing the harbor to forage on our side. While gators are common in these parts and normally don't bother humans, a big one like that can make a nice meal out of me. So I'm constantly searching the water for ripples or other disturbances that might indicate that I have company.

As I was completing my trimming on one section of the shoreline I happened to glance to my right and found a 4' gator floating right next to me. Instinct kicked in and I smacked him on the head with the flat side of my machete. He probably wouldn't cause me any trouble but the big bull could just as well be in the area hunting for his next snack.
They often eat smaller gators but I didn't want him to have to make a choice between the little one and big old me. Perhaps the camouflage worked well enough so that they couldn't see me.
text_fidelity_b: Men Waders Waterproof Chest Waders Bootfoot Chest Wader Light Hunting Fly Fishing Waders for Men with Boots Nylon/PVC Wader Camouflage/Brown 8-14

EKTOS 90% Woolen Blankets, 90" x 66", Warmest Blanket, Washable Wool Blanket, US Navy Blanket (Navy Blue) My dog likes to sit in my lap when we're by the campfire. I purchased this to cover her up and protect her from any stray sparks & pops. It is FABULOUS. We used our old blanket (an old synthetic bed cover) for years but it was in no way fire retardant and it took one good spark to make the blanket smoke. It was extinguished quickly but my dog was not comfortable near the fire afterwards. (I know it was ignorant to use a synthetic blanket next to a campfire but I grabbed it heading out the door for our first camping trip and since it worked didn't change it. DERP)

After our fiasco, my dog was scared of fire so I decided to purchase something wool and after careful consideration ended up with the Ektos blanket. Best purchase ever! She loves the blanket and is on my lap again. I love the blanket too. It is heavy but not overwhelming and not nearly as scratchy as other reviews made it out to be. Mind you, I'm not laying my bare skin against it. Bet it would be uncomfortable if I were wrapped in it half nekkid and sweating ...but I'm not, so it is perfect for what we're using it for. Both myself & my dog have piece of mind using this blanket as something of a campfire shield for her.

9/7/2018 Update

My husband used our campfire blanket as an extra layer to sleep in. He said it was perfect so I just ordered another blanket for him!

The original blanket I purchased is obviously still in great shape & being used regularly. I wash it on delicate and put it in the dryer on extra low. The first dry will produce a good deal of lint but the lint tapers off after that. It has been washed several times and has softened up a bit since purchase. I suspect we will end up purchasing a few more of these over the next few years since it is so hardy and versatile.

I would absolutely recommend this blanket others.

5/17/21 Update
...and I'm back to purchase yet another blanket! In a pinch, I had to use one of my campfire blankets in my hammock. It worked so well I am picking up another one to store with my hammock gear (along with another underquilt). Old Ektos are still go with us on every camping trip!

Skiboards Ski boards 99cm with Tyrolia releasable Bindings New set and they were awesome. This was my first experience with snow blades and I bought them on a whim. I am an experienced skier and usually opt for longer skis (180ish). The skis came pre-sharpened and waxed from the factory.

I took them out to Whiteface Mtn in New York. Took me about 2 hours to get used them and transition from normal skies. By the end of the day I was able to hit the double black diamonds and technical trails without any trouble. Snow blades are a bit different as they excel on packed powder, ice, and machine groomed snow (which, sadly, is what you usually get at most mountains on the east coast!). In light powder, the blades tend to sink due to the low amount of surface area, which slows you down. Additionally, I found that the blades were not as stable if you try to rocket straight down a hill- carving your way down is the best technique for snow blades.

Lastly, I found that the blades made it a bit harder to land jumps well. Since they aren't as long as normal skis, you don't have the same amount of forgiveness with your landings and need to make sure that you come down straight & balanced.

Overall, the skis are totally worth the price considering a regular pair of skis is easily 4x the cost.
text_fidelity_b: Skiboards Ski boards 99cm with Tyrolia releasable Bindings New set

text_fidelity_a:
Soozier Adjustable Seated Calf Raise Machine Leg Press Machine Strength Training Gym Equipment This calf raise machine is a great value piece of equipment for any home gym, on a budget. It's fairly comfortable, and allows you to easily do seated calf raises, and standing if you want to improvise a little bit. The big selling point is price, since many weight loaded seated calf machines are much more expensive for such a relatively simple movement. A big upside is there is pretty decent options for size adjustment to fit most people's needs.

The downsides are probably what allow the cost to be so low. While QC isn't necessarily bad, many pieces are not 'tight fitting', and need additional washers/spacers to make for a snug fit. Some pieces also needed to be manually widened so others would fit. Mechanically, this is a simplified seat calf machine, and takes several shortcuts in design that hurt QOL, such as the seat is mounted on the fulcrum, so you move as you perform the calf raise, and the handle to mount/unmount the machine from rest is on the rest-bar itself, in front of your knees, making it a little awkward to get in/out of. These are not deal breakers, but if you're used to 'gym-quality' equipment, this is does not meet the standard. However! it's so cheap that it doesn't even matter. Still get nasty calf pumps with this machine, 10/10 would buy again, as long as the price is cheap ~150$.
text_fidelity_b: Soozier Adjustable Seated Calf Raise Machine Leg Press Machine Strength Training Gym Equipment

text_fidelity_a:
LIGHTBAR | LED Headlamp, 300 to 500 Lumens, Spot Light Mode and Red Light Modes Available On Select Models - Perfect for Camping Running Biking Fishing Construction I've had this for a couple of months, but just used it for the first time this past weekend while camping with friends. I will never use it for that again.

A) The wide angle sounds like a good thing, but it was really annoying to my friends. I had to keep the headlamp at the lowest possible brightness, and even then the light shining so wide was still annoying to everyone around me.

B) The led strip is very thin, resulting in the light source being behind the plane of my glasses. So much light was reflecting off the lenses of my glasses back into my eyes that I truly couldn't see much of anything in front of me. There's no point lighting a path if I still can't actually see the path.

Also, this headlamp has a proprietary charger. So you have to keep that specific single-use cable with you in order to recharge the batteries. And the batteries drain even when not in use. I charged it fully when I first got it a couple of months ago. Fortunately I tested it before my camping trip and discovered it was completely drained. So you can't just charge it and expect it to be ready when you need it. I had to fully charge it just before I left.

It is really very bright, so if you need something really bright, and you don't have glasses, and there's no one else around you who might be blinded by your headlight, then it might be an ok choice for you. But with so very many options out there, I recommend you keep looking. There are definitely better choices than this.
text_fidelity_b: LIGHTBAR | LED Headlamp, 300 to 500 Lumens, Spot Light Mode and Red Light Modes Available On Select Models - Perfect for Camping Running Biking Fishing Construction

text_fidelity_a: FlipKlip Treadmill Book Holder 1-Pak This is a product that I want to love, and wants to be useful...and comes very close- but just misses the mark.  I use it for holding open those sheet music books that a certain music book publisher (I won't name names but it kinda rhymes with Cal Centered)seems to refuse to put in spiral bound form... ARRRGH nothing worse than trying to play a guitar when the book keeps closing on you.  I've tried everything I can think of to keep the pages open.  Closepins, those metal music stand arms, metal 3 pronged page clips, paperclips, spring clips.... heck even rubberbands.  This little gadget is probably the best solution so far (but not perfect). It will hold the book open (yea) but often times with sheet music you gotta flip back and forth between pages- this is difficult (not impossible, but does mess up the flow of the music).  The pins do hold well and have not ripped any pages so far- but they are a bit long and always seem to fall on the one note that I'm unsure of.  I kinda modified the way I use this by only clamping down on side of the book, leaving the other side loose so I can fip pages easier.  It works, but not perfectly.  If I were using this for straight up reading, it would be a 5 star no brainer, but for music....well it earned 4 stars (I'm feeling generous as this is the best solution I have found so far)
text_fidelity_b: FlipKlip Treadmill Book Holder 1-Pak

Just don't wabble on it too much, keep in mind this is a machine an care must be taken for users own safety.

text_fidelity_a: Platypus Platy 2-Liter Flexible Water Bottle For what it is, this is a really nifty vessel for drinking water from. I used it recently for a trip where I wanted to take only one backpack with all of my clothes and gear. While I *probably* could have crammed a water bottle in my bag, this definitely was a defining factor between making my bag too tightly jam-packed and just right. It becomes practically nothing and so lightweight when it's empty. Surprisingly, it stands well on its own when filled and due to the shape and rigidity of the sides, you can pick it up relatively comfortably and tilt it like a normal waterbottle. Of course, you can also only partially fill it, which makes it rather "flat" and slides into a small space on my backpack, which is great. It can make it a little more awkward to drink from. Ultimately, I wouldn't say this is "the best one handed water bottle" and it certainly isn't insulative and it surely can't be the most durable or the easiest to clean. But if you're just looking for a water bottle that can slip away into nothingness but be at the ready, I was more than happy to use this for a week+. Especially for the price. That being said, I was using the 1-litre bottle, which looks to be roughly the same design as the 2 but obviously more standard water bottle scale.
text_fidelity_b: Platypus Platy 2-Liter Flexible Water Bottle

WINGET 100% Carbon Fiber Cross X Country Ski Poles XC-100 I bought these intended to just use the baskets, handles and straps on another pole. I couldn't imagine the pole was very good, but I was pleasantly surprised. There are in fact 100% carbon as best I can tell. They are extremely stiff. Stiffer than my Rex R3 poles which set me back $150. They are heavier both in weight and noticeably in swing weight. I would suggest that these poles are equivalent to a $100 all carbon pole from Swix or Rex. I imagine that these were made by a manufacturer in China that produces for a name brand and then made these afterward. The only thing these poles lack is a brand. These are great workhorse poles for an experienced skier to use for rollerskiing or for sprint races (due to their stiffness). These would be a major upgrade for anyone who doesn't have 100% carbon poles. They probably aren't the best poles for marathons where an extremely light Swix pole would be better (but also cost north of $200).

Edit: The straps are rather small. Large male hands will fit but not well. You would need to buy new straps, but straps made by swix or rex would probably work fine.
text_fidelity_b: WINGET 100% Carbon Fiber Cross X Country Ski Poles XC-100

The pieces seem pretty durable, but you’d still want to be careful. I’m thinking there could be more convenient way of attachment to different size club shafts without actually having to change clips. The device does fit securely onto the clip and I had no indication of movement whatsoever. Initialization of the measurement process is very easy. While there’s an indicator light on the device when it’s ready for you to swing, the audible signal in the app is very useful. I used the app for iPhone. Once the swing has been made, then comes the analysis. The Help menu does a pretty good job of explaining things in the app, and the Description. Being able to manually toggle the “motion” views in the app is very cool. Various views available are also cool. All in all, I really like the device and the app. The ability to make notes on individual swings is very nice. I do, however, hope that Epson comes out the an iPad specific version of the app. I think that would make the app use experience better over just using an iPhone version on iPad. I’m in hopes that this device will help me to make some headway on my own in making improvements in my game. I really think it will.
text_fidelity_b: Epson M-Tracer MT500GII Golf Swing Analyzer
